readingGuide: `affectsCallLint` answers one narrow question: would adopting this delta change a byte CallLint SERVES or a verdict it EMITS? A delta can be normatively important upstream and still be scored `false` here, because CallLint is a stdio server with 13 tools and 19 read-only resources — it is not an HTTP transport, has no auth surface, and runs no long-lived tasks.

deltas.change: Per-request protocol version declaration via the `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` key in `_meta`, replacing initialize-only negotiation as the sole signal.
deltas.why: server.ts returns a single fixed protocolVersion at initialize (:61) and reads no per-request _meta. Adopting 2026-07-28 means honouring a per-request declaration and rejecting an unsupported one.

amendedByM26-1.supersedes: The `change` field above, specifically the phrase "replacing initialize-only negotiation as the sole signal". Retained verbatim because a deleted claim is indistinguishable from a claim never made — but a reader must take this amendment as current.
amendedByM26-1.asMeasured: 2026-07-28 does not DEMOTE `initialize`, it DELETES it. `grep -c 'nitialize'` over the vendored schema.ts is 0, and over schema.json is 0. changelog.snapshot.md Major changes #2 reads verbatim: "Make MCP stateless: remove the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake." The same changelog's Major #5 removes `ping` and `logging/setLevel` (both 0 hits in schema.ts).
amendedByM26-1.whyTheOriginalWasWrong: The phrase was authored before the bytes were vendored, from a rendered documentation page no gate could read back — the same mechanism that made F4's section names and F7's source URL wrong. Note the internal contradiction: this row's own citation, SEP-2575, IS the SEP that deletes the method the row describes as surviving.
amendedByM26-1.consequenceForScope: M26-1's recorded fix shape (`proposed-file-map.md`: "`initialize` must compare the requested version") targets a method that will not exist. So M26-1 as EXECUTED implements the negotiation layer only — per-request `_meta` read + UnsupportedProtocolVersionError — and leaves `initialize`/`ping` served, because REMOVING a served method is a public-surface change that needs `server/discover` (MUST implement upstream, owned by M26-2) to replace it. See ADR 0063 §2.
amendedByM26-1.landedBy: ADR 0063; gated by tests/invariants/mcp-spec-vendor.invariants.test.ts (both halves parsed) and packages/calllint-mcp/test/server.test.ts.

deltas.change: `MCP-Protocol-Version` header required on Streamable HTTP requests.
deltas.why: CallLint's MCP server is stdio-only (driven over stdin/stdout by scripts/mcp-pack-smoke.mjs:105). It exposes no HTTP transport, so no header applies.
The current error set (server.ts ERR.*) has no version-mismatch member, so a mismatched client today gets a generic error or a silent success at the wrong version.

deltas.change: `server/discover` — mandatory to implement, optional to call.
deltas.why: Not implemented today; the method table in server.ts handles initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read. 'Mandatory to implement' makes its absence a conformance gap the moment the version is advertised.

amendedByM26-2.supersedes: The `change` field above, which names TWO obligations where the locked bytes require FIVE, and the `(blocked by F8)` suffix on `owner`. Both retained verbatim rather than rewritten — a deleted claim is indistinguishable from a claim never made. Read this block as current.
amendedByM26-2.asMeasured: A conformant DiscoverResult requires FIVE fields, not two. From third_party/mcp-spec/2026-07-28/schema.json `required` arrays: DiscoverResult = ["cacheScope","capabilities","resultType","supportedVersions","ttlMs"], inherited via CacheableResult = ["cacheScope","resultType","ttlMs"] and Result = ["resultType"]; `additionalProperties` is ABSENT on all three. Separately, DiscoverRequest.params is NON-OPTIONAL (`params: RequestParams;`, schema.ts:667) and RequestParams requires `_meta`, whose RequestMetaObject requires TWO keys: `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` AND `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`. M26-1 shipped a reader for the second only.
amendedByM26-2.whyTheOriginalWasWrong: The row was authored from the changelog's one-line summary of SEP-2575, before the bytes were vendored. `resultType` is invisible in any description of discover because it is inherited from `Result` and required on EVERY result in this revision (it appears in 14 $defs); `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` are invisible because they come from CacheableResult and make discover a cacheable response — semantics quoted from HTTP Cache-Control, which CallLint had never decided anything about. Same mechanism as F4's section names, F7's source URL and D1's initialize premise: prose about a rendered page, unreadable by any gate.
amendedByM26-2.changelogAlsoWrong: changelog.snapshot.md:16 says discover advertises "supported protocol versions, capabilities, and identity". DiscoverResult has NO identity field — neither `serverInfo` nor `Implementation` appears in its $defs entry. Identity is ResultMetaObject["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]? (schema.ts:157): optional, a SHOULD, and warned against for security decisions. A reader implementing from that sentence would put serverInfo in the result body, where the schema does not define it.
amendedByM26-2.resultTypeIsOpen: `export type ResultType = "complete" | "input_required" | string;` (schema.ts:216), and schema.json gives it a bare {"type":"string"} with no `enum` and no `const`. So no closed-set gate over its value is possible; the gate asserts the OPENNESS instead.
amendedByM26-2.consequenceForScope: M26-2 implements the method and emits all five required fields, but `resultType` goes on THIS result only — at 2024-11-05 its absence is the DEFINED behaviour ("the client MUST treat the absent field as `complete`"), so adding it to the other eight results would change bytes today's clients already receive for a revision we do not claim. `ttlMs: 0` / `cacheScope: "private"` are the inert ends of both enums, not a caching strategy. `clientCapabilities` is deliberately unread: at 2024-11-05 there is no `_meta` at all, so a strict read would reject every request today's clients send. See ADR 0064 §4 and §5.
amendedByM26-2.landedBy: ADR 0064; gated by tests/invariants/mcp-spec-vendor.invariants.test.ts (which reads the `required` arrays off disk and checks server.ts against them, rather than restating the five names), packages/calllint-mcp/test/server.test.ts, and a 7th stdio request in scripts/mcp-pack-smoke.mjs that proves the method answers from the published tarball.
amendedByM26-2.stillNotClaimed: PROTOCOL_VERSION remains 2024-11-05 and 2026-07-28 remains absent from SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS. M-OPEN-5 orders the public claim LAST — after (a) this method and (b) removing the handshake. Only (a) is done.

deltas.change: Long-running task lifecycle, opt-in via initialization negotiation.
deltas.why: Every CallLint tool is a synchronous pure delegator returning one result (ADR 0025). There is no long-running work to model, and declining the extension is conformant.
